title: Image build broken: apps/common + apps/generic go.mod stale after rclone 1.75.1 bump
body:
The rclone 1.75.1 bump (#744) ran `go mod tidy` in **core** only. `apps/common` and `apps/generic` `replace ../core`, so core's new transitive deps (aws-sdk-go-v2 bumps + new indirects) were never recorded in their go.sum. Under the Dockerfile's `-mod=readonly`, the `build-web` stage fails:

```
go: updates to go.mod needed, disabled by -mod=readonly; to update it: go mod tidy
ERROR: ... go build -o /out/backupd-web ./cmd/backupd-web ... exit code: 1
```

So `container/Dockerfile` (and CI's uibundle/dockercli image-build tests) cannot build main. Fix: `go mod tidy` in apps/common + apps/generic. Found while building the debug image for the NAS troubleshooting session.

title: fix: NULL cells render as blank, indistinguishable from empty string
body:
## Description
`App::submit` converts each `db_core::engine::Cell` to a `String` via the generic `ToString` before building the results `Grid` (`grid_pane.rs`). `Cell::Display`'s "NULL renders as empty" is correct and deliberate for db-core's shell-style clients (sqlite-rs, column-rs, loglume all share it, matching `sqlite3`'s own CLI convention) -- but a TUI grid isn't a shell pipe, and losing the NULL/empty-string distinction there means a sparse result set (e.g. `SELECT *` over a `.log` file's Tier-3 columns, where most fields don't apply to most rows) is indistinguishable from one full of empty strings.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a `.log` file with heterogeneous per-line fields (e.g. `examples/iot-fleet/fixture/device.log`)
2. `SELECT * FROM log`
3. Observe: rows where a field like `firmware` doesn't apply render as a blank cell, identical to how an actual empty string would render

## Suggested approach
Special-case `Cell::Null` before stringifying in `App::submit` (or wherever `Cell` -> `Grid` cell conversion happens), rendering it as a distinct marker (e.g. `<NULL>`, dimmed via `theme::subtext()`) instead of an empty string -- the common convention across GUI/TUI SQL clients (DataGrip, rainfrog, etc).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `Cell::Null` value renders as a visually distinct marker in the results grid, not a blank cell
- [ ] A real empty string (`Cell::Text(String::new())`) still renders as genuinely blank, not also marked -- the two must stay visually distinguishable
- [ ] Existing tests (grid_pane, app submit tests) still pass; a new test covers the NULL-vs-empty-string distinction

## Additional Notes
db-core's `Cell::Display` itself is out of scope -- it's correct for every other client sharing it.

title: Default window is taller than the work area on a scaled display, so pen input under the taskbar is discarded
body:
The default window is taller than the work area on a scaled display, so part of it sits under the taskbar — and **pen input aimed at that region is silently discarded** while the window carries on running and painting.

Found by `--selftest`, which fails on it today:

```
[FAIL] L0.window-placement  client 3712x2025 at 124,175; work area 3840x2052 at 0,0  <- input outside the work area is silently discarded
```

## The arithmetic

`MainWindow.axaml` declares `Width="1650" Height="900"`. Those are DIPs, so the physical height is `900 × scale`:

| display | scale | window height | work area | fits? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4K | 2.25× | 2025px | 2052px | **27px of slack** — any centering or cascade pushes it under |
| 1440p | 1.75× | 1575px | 1356px | **no — 219px over** |

The 1440p row is the one that matters: that is the display used for drawing, and the window cannot fit on it at all at the declared size.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than ignoring

Injected and real pen input are both delivered by absolute screen position. A window region below the work area receives nothing — no points, no telemetry, no error. The app looks healthy and the lower part of the canvas just does not draw, which reads as a bug in whatever is being tested rather than as a placement problem.

This cost real time earlier in the investigation: a window straddling two monitors ran to y=2214 against a work area ending at 2052, and strokes in the bottom 162px produced nothing while identical strokes higher up worked. That presents exactly like "the lower canvas is broken".

## Options

1. **Clamp at startup** — measure the target monitor's work area and shrink to fit. Handles every display without guessing, and handles the multi-monitor case where the right answer differs per screen.
2. **Smaller default** — pick a height that fits the smallest display in use. Simple; needs revisiting when the hardware changes.
3. **Leave it, exempt the check** — if 1650×900 is deliberate, `L0.window-placement` needs a documented exemption, otherwise `--selftest` fails by default and stops being a usable gate.

Option 1 is the most robust. Whichever is chosen, it is a visible change to the app's appearance, which is why it is filed rather than done.

## Related

The same class of problem was fixed in `Scribble.Rust` in [WinPenKit#20](https://github.com/TheSevenPens/WinPenKit/pull/20) by reducing its default height — its 700-point window was 1575px at 2.25× and did not survive the window manager cascading it down a few launches.

Worth deciding once and applying to both repos, since the reasoning is identical and the trap is not obvious from reading either app's XAML: nothing at the declaration site suggests that a height in DIPs becomes a placement bug at some scale factor.

Note also that `L0.window-placement` is sensitive to where the window manager happens to put the window, so it can pass or fail across runs at a borderline size. That flakiness is documented in [WinPenKit Docs/SELF-TEST.md](https://github.com/TheSevenPens/WinPenKit/blob/main/Docs/SELF-TEST.md) and is a second reason to resolve this rather than live with it.

title: fix(agents): ship.sh auto-merge gate punishes the correct link word
body:
The gate reads the link WORD when it should count the issue REFERENCES.

```bash
[[ "$link_word" == "Closes" && "$mergeable" == "MERGEABLE" ]] && auto_ok="yes"
```

`AGENTS.md` § PR convention authorizes auto-merge on (a) CI green, (b) the PR closes a single issue, (c) no conflicts. Condition (b) got implemented as a literal string comparison rather than as what it means.

## Why that is backwards

The danger condition (b) exists for is documented in this same script: an epic closed by its first phase dies with the remaining phases unwritten. That is the danger of `Closes` on an epic. `Part of` is the CORRECT link word for a phase — and `Part of` closes nothing, so merging one cannot kill anything.

So the gate refuses to merge precisely because the author chose the safe word. Do the prudent thing, lose the automation.

Hit on PR #963 (`Part of #921`, CI green, MERGEABLE, CLEAN): the orchestrator correctly reported it could not merge, and a human ran `gh pr merge` by hand. That manual step is what this line of work exists to remove.

## The case that SHOULD block

There is one, and it is a different case. When the commits reference several issue numbers, pre-flight already auto-demotes to `Part of` and warns that it guessed. That PR has ambiguous scope — nobody stated which issue it belongs to. Blocking there is right. A deliberate `--part-of` naming one epic is not that case.

## Fix

Track whether the link word was reached by demotion, and gate on that instead of on the word:

- exactly one issue referenced (explicit `--issue`/`--part-of`/`--closes`, or auto-detected singular) then auto-merge is allowed
- several issues referenced then refuse, a human decides

`mergeable == MERGEABLE` and CI green stay required. Only condition (b) changes, and it changes to what it already meant.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `--part-of` naming one issue auto-merges on green
- [ ] `--closes` behaviour unchanged
- [ ] commits referencing several issues still refuse, with the reason
- [ ] the refusal message names which condition failed

Follows from #948. Found on #963/#921.

title: [P1] DBF writers accept invalid calendar text in Date fields
body:
## Problem

The shared DBF field writer claims to require `YYYYMMDD` or `YYYY-MM-DD`, but its Date (`D`) branch only removes every hyphen and checks that eight bytes remain.

At audited commit `820b1b93afa5d9083b4093aa9c581b7ceb54da1a`:

- [`src/vfp/dbf_table.cpp#L1047-L1056`](https://github.com/rhamenator/Project-Copperfin/blob/820b1b93afa5d9083b4093aa9c581b7ceb54da1a/src/vfp/dbf_table.cpp#L1047-L1056)
- [`resources/locales/en-US/strings.json#L1529`](https://github.com/rhamenator/Project-Copperfin/blob/820b1b93afa5d9083b4093aa9c581b7ceb54da1a/resources/locales/en-US/strings.json#L1529)

Consequently, values such as `abcdefgh`, `99999999`, `20230229`, and strings with hyphens in arbitrary positions can be persisted as DBF Date bytes. The first is not numeric, the second has impossible month/day components, the third is not a valid Gregorian date, and arbitrary hyphen placement does not match either documented input shape.

`write_field_bytes()` is shared by table creation, append, replace, and the dBASE III writer, so this is not confined to one export command. It can produce files that downstream dBASE/FoxPro-compatible readers reject or reinterpret, while Copperfin reports the write as successful. The only test reference to `DateValueInvalid` is localization-catalog parity; there is no behavioral validation of the accepted Date grammar or calendar range.

This is the Date-field sibling of #5677, which tracks arbitrary text in Numeric fields, and is not covered by that issue's numeric-only scope.

## Completion criteria

- Accept only the intended empty/null forms and exact `YYYYMMDD` or `YYYY-MM-DD` syntax for Date writes.
- Require ASCII decimal digits in all date components and reject invalid Gregorian dates, including month/day range errors and non-leap-year February 29.
- Reject misplaced, missing, or extra separators rather than erasing hyphens before validation.
- Cover the shared create, append, and replace paths (including dBASE III creation) and verify an invalid value leaves an existing table or destination artifact unchanged.
- Add boundary tests for leap years, month lengths, blank/null dates, both valid input spellings, non-digits, and malformed separators.

title: The identifier stamp hashes its key material, so no FerroEHR-minted id attests to its licence
body:
Verified 2026-09-12 against the hosted sandbox running 4.2.0 and against a local run of the released `ghcr.io/rubentalstra/ferroehr:4.2.0` image: `GET /rest/status` reports the embedded non-commercial grant correctly (`state: licensed`, `use: non-commercial`, licensee "Everyone, under the Business Source License 1.1", `not_after: 2099-12-31`, `configured_token: absent`; the embedded token is byte-identical to the register's `01a090a8-59e4-76da-92f5-3f7e4ea9d7c0` token), but `ferrolicence attest` over server-minted identifiers (a fresh `POST /ehr`, a composition's versioned-object id) matches **0 of N** for both candidates, the licence key and the unlicensed constant. A probe test inside this repository confirms the cause is not the wiring: `LicenceState::load_now` yields the licence with id `01a090a8-…`, `stamp_key().mint()` produces an id that `StampKey::for_licence(01a090a8-…).carries` in THIS crate, and the same id fails an independent HMAC-SHA256 computation of the design.

`app/ferroehr/src/licence/stamp.rs` deviates from the licensing design in two places:

1. `StampKey::new` uses `SHA-256(material)` as the HMAC key. The design (and the attestation tooling that reads the register) keys the HMAC with the raw material: `"ferroehr/licence/v1/" ‖ licence_id` (16 raw bytes), or the public unlicensed constant. HMAC pads a key shorter than the block size itself, so hashing first produces a different key and a different tag for every identifier. The crate's own test `the_key_is_hmac_over_the_sha256_of_the_material` pins the deviation rather than the design.
2. The fail-safe constant is `"ferroehr/no-licence/v1"`; the design names the public unlicensed key `"ferroehr/unlicensed/v1"`.

Consequence: every identifier minted by 4.2.0 is unattestable, so the whole point of the stamp (telling an unlicensed or altered build apart from a licensed one from a sample of ids) does not hold for this release. The wire and the stored data are otherwise unaffected: the stamp lives in the two CSPRNG bytes of a version-7 UUID, so changing the key changes only which ids future mints produce; ids minted under 4.2.0 stay valid identifiers and simply carry no recognisable stamp.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `StampKey::new` keys the HMAC with the raw material and the fail-safe constant equals the design's public unlicensed key; the deviating test is replaced by known-answer tests computed independently (unlicensed key at `timestamp_ms = 1000` → `12 1e`; licence `01a090a8-59e4-76da-92f5-3f7e4ea9d7c0` at `1000` → `49 51`; licence `0192a7e1-2345-7000-8000-000000000000` at `0x0192a7e12345` → `9e 8a`).
- [ ] `ferrolicence attest` over identifiers minted by a build carrying the fix identifies the embedded non-commercial licence (recorded here from a local run).
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` entry under Fixed stating that identifiers minted by 4.2.0 carry no recognisable stamp.

## Why this card exists

**#1553 closed with 2 of its 4 boxes unmet.** PR #1554 merged at `2026-09-12T05:41:14Z` with

This is the #1285 shape #1313 was written to stop: *"closed with 2 of 7 items unlanded and
untracked, which is why #1357 existed."* Filing rather than reopening, per `docs/WORKFLOW.md` —
closed is closed.

Boxes 1 and 3 on #1553 have been un-ticked to match what `main` actually does.

## What landed, and what did not

Measured against `origin/main` @ `1818fdde`:

| #1553 box | on `main` | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 — a multi-file fixture carrying the marker compiles and is asserted | **met** | `tests/bugs/issue-1553-no-warnings-multifile/` |

| 1 — *one* derivation of where a fixture's headers live | **not met** | `git show origin/main:scripts/test-utils.ts \| grep -c 'join(rootDir, "tests/include")'` → **4** |
| 3 — a warning in a helper reddens the fixture | **not met** | `validateNoWarnings(cFile, rootDir)` takes one path; no helper translation unit is ever compiled |

Reviewed on #1554 and fixed in two commits that did not reach `main`:

   is already in scope at the call site. Blast radius measured: **2** helper implementations

2. **`[important]` Four copies, not one derivation.** The include pair — and
   `-Wno-unused-variable` / `-Wno-main` with it — is spelled out at four gcc call sites. Two of

5. **`[moderate]` No test asserts a helper implementation is compiled at all** — the one
   assertion that would catch (1).
6. **`[moderate]` `lib.cnx`'s comment describes a compile that does not happen**, and ADR-043

- [ ] #1553's boxes 1 and 3 are satisfied by `main`, and re-ticked there with the measurement

只读解析真实会话 `20260912-133315-f980`：4 个任务、14 条消息、含工具定义约 10535 tokens，`CONTEXT_KEEP_RECENT_TOKENS=20000`。压缩规则是「退休超出保留窗口的旧内容」，历史比保留窗口还小，切点落在第一条消息之前，因此没有内容可退休。

1. `/compact` 不带参数时，至少退休比当前任务更旧的全部原文；历史短于保留窗口也能用。
2. `/compact <token>` 指定本次保留的 token 数，仍只落在任务或轮边界上。
3. 回执带数字：`[压缩/manual] 10535 -> 1830 tokens；退休 8 条旧消息（收起 3 个工具结果）；方法=model；保留窗口=2000`；未压缩时说明历史与保留窗口。
4. 参数非法时打印用法，不改变上下文。

## 验证

- 服务层用例：短历史下退休旧任务、显式保留量按数字切、只有一个任务时不改动并报告数字。
- Agent 层用例：两个任务后 `/compact` 只退休第一个任务、保留第二个任务的原文，`--resume` 重放一致。
- 真实会话只读核对：切点从 1 变为 12（当前任务起点），可退休 11 条原始消息。

title: feat(helm): configure dedicated context roots and path-based ingress for OpenAPI viewer, MinIO, and Keycloak in infra chart
body:
### User Story / Objective
As an operator and developer deploying `vuhive-cloud-infra` behind an Ingress controller (e.g., Traefik, Ingress NGINX) or reverse proxy under a unified domain (or localhost), I want the OpenAPI viewer (Swagger UI), MinIO (Console and S3 API), and Keycloak IAM services to run with configurable context roots (subpaths/prefixes), so that path-based ingress routing rules can route traffic cleanly without URL rewrites, asset loading failures, or redirect loops.

---

### Background & Context
In `deploy/helm/vuhive-cloud-infra`, infrastructure components are deployed as standalone or subchart workloads:
1. **OpenAPI Viewer (`openapiViewer`)**: Swagger UI is currently configured to serve from root `/`. While `openapi-viewer-ingress.yaml` exists, Swagger UI's web assets and API spec fetching default to `/` rather than respecting a subpath (e.g., `/docs` or `/swagger-ui`). In the official `swaggerapi/swagger-ui` container image, the `BASE_URL` environment variable governs the HTTP prefix.
2. **Keycloak (`keycloak`)**: In `keycloak-deployment.yaml`, `KC_HTTP_RELATIVE_PATH` is currently hardcoded to `"/"`. When routing Keycloak through an Ingress with a path prefix (e.g., `/auth` or `/keycloak`), Keycloak requires `KC_HTTP_RELATIVE_PATH` to match the path prefix so that realm endpoints, OIDC discovery (`.well-known/openid-configuration`), admin console, and browser redirects preserve the context root. Additionally, the infra chart currently lacks a dedicated Ingress template for Keycloak.
3. **MinIO (`minio`)**: MinIO exposes both an S3 API (default port `9000`) and a Browser Console (default port `9001`). When exposing MinIO via a shared Ingress hostname using path-based routing, MinIO Console must support context root / subpath configuration (e.g., `/minio/ui` or `/minio/console` via `CONSOLE_SUBPATH` or `MINIO_BROWSER_REDIRECT_URL`), and MinIO S3 API can route under a dedicated path prefix (e.g., `/s3` or `/minio/api`).

Currently, attempting path-based Ingress routing under a single hostname (e.g., `http://vuhive.local/docs`, `http://vuhive.local/auth`, `http://vuhive.local/minio`) causes path mismatches, broken asset references, and redirect loops because each service assumes it owns the root context (`/`).

---

### Key Requirements & Tasks

#### 1. OpenAPI Viewer Context Root & Ingress Alignment
- Add configurable context root setting in `deploy/helm/vuhive-cloud-infra/values.yaml` (e.g., `openapiViewer.contextPath: "/docs"` or `openapiViewer.basePath`).
- Update `openapi-viewer-deployment.yaml`:
  - Pass `BASE_URL` container environment variable configured to the context path when specified.
  - Update `livenessProbe` and `readinessProbe` `httpGet.path` to probe the configured context root.
- Update `openapi-viewer-ingress.yaml` to route requests matching the configured context path.

#### 2. Keycloak Relative Path & Ingress Support
- Expose `keycloak.httpRelativePath` in `values.yaml` (e.g., defaulting to `"/"` and configurable to `"/auth"` or `"/keycloak"`).
- Update `keycloak-deployment.yaml` to dynamically set `KC_HTTP_RELATIVE_PATH` from `.Values.keycloak.httpRelativePath`.
- Ensure Keycloak health probes on the management port (port `9000`, `/health/live`, `/health/ready`) or HTTP port correctly respect or isolate from the relative path.
- Add an optional Ingress manifest `templates/keycloak-ingress.yaml` (with `keycloak.ingress.enabled`, `hosts`, `paths`, `annotations`, `tls`) to route incoming path-based traffic to the Keycloak Service.
- Ensure realm configurations and BFF OIDC integration documentation / helper URLs account for the context root.

#### 3. MinIO Console & API Path-Based Ingress Configuration
- Configure MinIO subchart values in `vuhive-cloud-infra/values.yaml` to support context paths:
  - Configure `minio.consoleIngress` with path-based routing (e.g., path `/minio/ui` or `/minio/console`).
  - Pass `MINIO_BROWSER_REDIRECT_URL` and/or `CONSOLE_SUBPATH` via `minio.environment` so the console UI renders static assets and redirects under the designated context root.
  - Configure `minio.ingress` for S3 API path routing if desired.

#### 4. Documentation & Local Validation
- Update `deploy/helm/vuhive-cloud-infra/README.md` with:
  - Clear examples of configuring path-based ingress rules under a single host.
  - Recommended context paths (e.g., `/docs` for OpenAPI Viewer, `/auth` for Keycloak, `/minio` for MinIO Console).
  - Browser accessibility notes for local development (e.g., `/docs` fetching `/openapi.json` from the control plane).
- Verify with `helm lint` and `helm template` across default, disabled, and path-customized configurations.

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `openapiViewer` supports a configurable context path via `BASE_URL` and adapts probes and Ingress paths accordingly.
- [ ] `keycloak` dynamically reads `KC_HTTP_RELATIVE_PATH` from Helm values and renders an optional Ingress resource for path-based routing.
- [ ] `minio` console can be accessed via a path prefix without broken static assets or redirect loops.
- [ ] Helm chart templates render valid Kubernetes manifests (`helm lint` and `helm template` pass cleanly) when context roots and Ingresses are enabled.
- [ ] `deploy/helm/vuhive-cloud-infra/README.md` documents path-based Ingress configuration with examples.

title: feat(observability): stateful health probe logging on status change
body:
### User Story / Objective
As a platform engineer or SRE operating `vuhive-cloud` (control plane server and Go BFF) in Kubernetes clusters, I want health and liveness/readiness probes to only emit logs when their evaluated health status changes (e.g., from initial state to healthy, healthy to degraded/unhealthy, or degraded/unhealthy to recovered), so that application logs are not flooded with repetitive, redundant probe log lines during normal operation while still alerting operators immediately upon state degradation or recovery.

### Background & Context
Currently, Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes query `/healthz` and `/api/v1/health` periodically (e.g., every 5–10 seconds) on both the Control Plane server (`cmd/server`) and the Go BFF (`cmd/bff`).
Because both components register global `LoggingMiddleware` and the BFF client performs HTTP logging for every upstream `/healthz` request:
- Every probe request produces `Debug` and `Info` log lines ("incoming HTTP request", "completed HTTP request", "handled http request", "checking upstream control plane health", "completed control plane health check").
- In high-density or long-running environments, health probe log noise dominates log streams, inflating log storage costs, increasing log ingestion volume, and obscuring meaningful application events.

Instead, health probes should maintain state across evaluations and log only when the final status changes:
- **Good Final Status (Healthy / 200 OK)**: Log at `Info` level upon initial healthy transition or when recovering from an unhealthy state.
- **Bad Final Status (Degraded / Unhealthy / Non-200 / Error)**: Log at `Warn` level when transitioning from healthy to unhealthy or upon initial failure.
- **Unchanged Status**: Suppress logging so that repetitive health checks remain completely silent while status is steady.

### Key Requirements & Tasks
1. **Control Plane Server (`internal/adapters/inbound/rest`)**:
   - Update HTTP router/middleware logging to recognize health probe endpoints (`/healthz`, `/api/v1/health`).
   - Track health probe state transitions (initial / healthy / unhealthy) in a thread-safe manner.
   - Emit an `Info` log when health status transitions to good (e.g., startup initial OK or recovery).
   - Emit a `Warn` log when health status transitions to bad (e.g., status code >= 400 or failure).
   - Suppress redundant logging when status remains unchanged.
2. **Go BFF (`internal/bff/adapters/inbound/rest` and `internal/bff/adapters/outbound/controlplane`)**:
   - Update BFF `/healthz` endpoint handler and middleware to avoid logging repetitive unchanged probe results.
   - Update the outbound `ControlPlaneClient.CheckHealth` method to only log when the upstream control plane status transitions (log `Info` on healthy transition/recovery, `Warn` on failure/degraded status).
3. **Thread Safety & Edge Cases**:
   - Ensure state transition tracking is atomic or protected by mutexes (`sync.RWMutex` or `atomic.Int32`) across concurrent probe requests.
   - Isolate health probe logging state per probe target / endpoint to avoid cross-endpoint state collision.
4. **Unit & Integration Tests**:
   - Add unit tests verifying:
     - First request logs `Info` on 200 OK.
     - Subsequent consecutive 200 OK requests produce zero log output.
     - Transition from 200 OK to failure logs `Warn`.
     - Subsequent consecutive failures produce zero duplicate log output.
     - Transition from failure back to 200 OK logs `Info`.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Health probe endpoints (`/healthz`, `/api/v1/health`) in Control Plane (`cmd/server`) log only on status change (Info on good status, Warn on bad status).
- [ ] Health probe endpoint (`/healthz`) and upstream health check in BFF (`cmd/bff`) log only on status change (Info on good status, Warn on bad status).
- [ ] Repetitive consecutive health checks with the same status do not generate log entries.
- [ ] Thread-safe concurrent execution without race conditions verified by `go test -race`.
- [ ] All existing test suites pass cleanly.

title: CI runs the full Flutter build on documentation-only pull requests
body:
## Measured

`ci.yml` has no path filter, so the heavy job runs on every pull request. On two that touched no file under `app/`:

| PR | Files under `app/` | "Analyze, test & build APK" |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #35 (the site) | 0 | **421 s** |
| #36 (the README) | 0 | **399 s** |

Seven minutes of Flutter build to validate Markdown. It will get worse now that work is batched, since a release lot mixes documentation with code.

`pages.yml` is **not** part of the problem: it already filters on `docs/**`, `tool/validate_registry.py` and its own file, and has run four times, each on a push that genuinely touched the site.

## The trap in the obvious fix

Adding `paths-ignore` at the workflow level would break every documentation pull request, permanently.

Both job names are **required status checks** on `main`:

```
Analyze, test & build APK
Validate the counter registry
```

A workflow skipped by a path filter never reports its checks. GitHub then waits for a status that will never arrive and the pull request stays blocked with no way forward — the same class of failure as the job rename that left #16 stuck.

## The shape that works

Keep the trigger as it is, so the checks always report, and move the decision **inside** the job:

1. A first step computes whether anything under `app/` or `android/` changed.
2. The expensive steps — `pub get`, codegen check, `analyze`, `test`, `build apk` — become conditional on it.
3. The job still runs and still reports success under the same name, in seconds rather than minutes.

Worth deciding at the same time: whether a change to `.github/workflows/**` should count as touching the app. It should — a workflow edit that breaks the build ought to be caught by the build.

`Validate the counter registry` takes 4–6 s and is a safety net on the file every install downloads. Leave it running unconditionally.

## Not worth doing

Filtering Dependabot runs. A dependency bump must go through the full build; that is the entire point of it.

title: /cloud/ 把「需要有 GitHub Actions」从门槛改成杠杆：CI 里放什么决定 Orbi 保证什么
body:
## 问题

`/cloud/` 现在这句（`site/pages/cloud/index.html`，及 `site/pages/zh/cloud/index.html` 镜像）：

> Releases are never automatic. You open the release Issue and apply the `ai-release` label — a label only humans set — and **your repository needs GitHub Actions, because the release's test acceptance IS the CI result.**

中文版：

> 发版从不是全自动。你开一张 release 票并打上 ai-release 标签——这个标签只有人能打——而且**目标仓库要有 GitHub Actions，因为发版的测试验收就是 CI 结果**。

**事实没错，但framing 是反的。** 现在读起来是「你得先满足一个条件才能用我们」，是门槛；实际它是这个产品最有杠杆的一句话——**用户在 CI 里放什么测试，决定了 Orbi 替他保证什么**。

## 为什么现在改

2026-09-12 一位重度 AI 用户（3.1K 曝光那条推）从「不敢合并代码、总觉得它在忽悠我」到「验证了一天，合并了」，中间加的就是一轮 **playwright 全自动 e2e**。

他的「不敢」不是心理问题，是缺一道自动跑完的验证门。而 Orbi 的门禁本来就读 CI 的 check run conclusion——**他那道门，我们现在就能读**。这件事官网一个字没说。

详见 [反馈存档 #270](https://github.com/orbi-build/orbi-cloud/discussions/270)；配套的完整说明页是 #128。

## 改法

把「needs GitHub Actions」从条件句改成能力句，并链到 #128 那一页。方向（文案由交付时定稿，不必逐字照抄）：

> 发版的测试验收就是你仓库的 CI 结果——**所以 CI 里放什么，决定了 Orbi 替你保证什么**：放单测，它保证代码逻辑；放业务流程的 e2e，它保证的是业务闭环。[怎么接 →](/guides/ci-gates/)

英文同理，保持与现有页面语气一致。

## 边界（不能因为改成正面说法就省掉）

**没有任何 check run 时两道门禁都放行**，代码原文：

- `runner.py`：`if not check_runs: ... "no check runs (nothing to gate)"`
- `release.py`：`... "no check runs on {release_commit} (nothing to gate)"`

即**无 CI 的仓库能跑通，但失去唯一的测试验收闸门**。这句话在 `/cloud/` 上至少要有一句，细节留给 #128。

## 验收

- [ ] `/cloud/` 与 `/zh/cloud/` 两处同步改，语气一致
- [ ] 链接指向 `/guides/ci-gates/`（依赖 #128；#128 未上线前本票可先改 framing、暂不加链接，二者不互相阻塞）
- [ ] 「无 CI 则失去测试闸门」这层意思在页面上没有丢
- [ ] 现有 smoke 断言若断到这段文案，同步更新

title: [1.8.5] co browser config: a default engine, and the paid one is called WTF Browser
body:
## Outcome

Two things about choosing a browser engine.

**A default you set once.** Today the paid engine needs `--engine onion` on every single invocation. Someone testing the WTF Browser on their own machine types it a hundred times a day, and an agent driving `co browser` has to carry it through every call site — which is exactly where it gets forgotten, and the run silently uses system Chrome instead of the thing under test.

```bash
co browser config                 # what the default is, and where it came from
co browser config wtf             # make the paid engine the default here
co browser config system          # back to free
```

**A name that matches the product.** The paid engine is called the **WTF Browser** everywhere a person reads it — the help text says so in the same line that spells the flag `onion`. `--engine onion` is the internal word leaking into the interface.

```
co browser --engine onion <function>   # pay for the WTF Browser (default: system Chrome)
                      ^^^^^                 ^^^^^^^^^^^
```

## The safety property this touches, stated plainly

`useful_tools/browser_tools/engine.py` currently guarantees that `auto` and `system` "return before importing Onionwright, loading a token, calling the server, or touching the paid cache: the default engine is the installed system Chrome, and money is never spent unless the caller asks."

A configured default breaks the second half of that sentence: `co browser go_to x.com` would spend money without that invocation asking. That is the point of the feature and it must not be silent. So:

- The setting is written by an explicit command that says what it costs before writing it.
- Every session the config sends to the paid engine says so in its output — the reason string becomes `wtf_configured`, not `wtf_ready`, so the account's own record shows which invocations were a standing choice rather than a request.
- `--engine system` always wins over the config, so there is a way to not spend money that does not require editing a file.
- The default default is unchanged: with nothing configured, it is system Chrome.

## Where the setting lives

`CO_BROWSER_ENGINE` in the selected env file, which is `~/.co/keys.env` unless `--env-file` says otherwise. Reasons to reuse that rather than invent a browser config file:

- `co env` already answers "what does this machine hold and where did it come from", including which values the shell overrides — which is the question someone debugging a wrong engine will ask.
- One file to copy to another machine, and `co deploy` already carries it.
- `CO_BROWSER_ENGINE=system co browser …` works for one command without a flag, which is what a script wants.

`co browser config` is the front door that writes it and explains the cost; the variable is the mechanism. Both are documented.

## Naming

`wtf` becomes the name. `onion` keeps working as a deprecated alias at the CLI boundary and says so once, the way `co feishu serve` now points at `consume`.

The wire value between client and daemon stays `onion` in 1.8.x. Renaming it would make a 1.8.5b1 daemon and a later client disagree about what they are launching, and the engine value is what `remote_egress` checks to decide whether a paid session may carry traffic — not a string to churn for tidiness. That is a rename to do in 1.9 with both sides moving together, and it is invisible to anyone reading the CLI.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `co browser config` with no argument prints the current default and its source (unset / env file / shell)
- [ ] `co browser config wtf|system|auto` writes `CO_BROWSER_ENGINE` through the same path as `co env set`
- [ ] With nothing configured the default is still system Chrome, and a test asserts it
- [ ] `--engine` beats the config; `--engine system` beats a configured `wtf`
- [ ] A paid session chosen by config is distinguishable in its own output from one chosen by a flag
- [ ] `--engine wtf` works, `--engine onion` works and names the new spelling once
- [ ] Every user-facing string that says "onion" where it means the product says WTF Browser
- [ ] `co browser config` is in `--help` and has a next-step tip

## A rule for cli-skill-design

This is the second time a frequently-repeated flag has turned out to be the real defect rather than the feature it guards (the first was `--engine` itself being required for every paid call). The skill should say it: **a setting a caller repeats on every invocation belongs in configuration, and the flag is the override.** An agent that has to carry a flag through twenty call sites will drop it at one of them, and the failure is silent — the wrong thing runs and reports success.

body:
## Goal

A split parent lists its pieces as GitHub sub-issues and shows completed-of-total; an item that depends on another carries a blocked-by relation to it; `issue-next` skips an item whose blockers are open by reading that relation. The `Depends on #N` line stays in § Related as the readable form, written from the relation.

## Why

A dependency reaches the tracker as prose and nothing else:

- `claude/skills/issue-write/SKILL.md:24` defines a dependency as a body line, `Depends on #4, #7`; `:49` creates the item with `gh issue create` and makes no relation.
- `claude/skills/issue-triage/SKILL.md:88` — the split ruling creates the pieces through `issue-write`, then `gh issue edit <N> --body-file <path>` gives the parent's § Related one dependency line naming them. Nothing links parent to piece.
- `claude/skills/issue-next/SKILL.md:29` — the skip walks each number the body line names with `gh issue view <N> --json state`. The body line is the only source.

The relations exist on this tracker and nothing here uses them. `gh api graphql` against princejonn/ai-config, 2026-09-12:

- #54, split into #60 and #61: `subIssues.totalCount 0`, `subIssuesSummary {total 0, completed 0}`; #60 and #61 both return `parent null`.
- #63, whose § Related carries `- Depends on #62.`: `blockedBy.totalCount 0` on #63, `blocking.totalCount 0` on #62.

`gh issue list` prints number, title, labels and updated-at — no body — so a dependency is invisible until a skill parses the body.

Schema introspection on this machine, same date:

- `Issue` fields present: `subIssues`, `subIssuesSummary`, `parent`, `blockedBy`, `blocking`.
- Mutations present: `addSubIssue`, `removeSubIssue`, `reprioritizeSubIssue`, `addBlockedBy`, `removeBlockedBy`.
- `AddSubIssueInput` fields: `issueId`, `subIssueId`, `subIssueUrl`, `replaceParent`, `clientMutationId`.
- `AddBlockedByInput` fields: `issueId`, `blockingIssueId`, `clientMutationId`.

Every field and mutation the § Proposal names is confirmed to exist, so no REST route is needed.

## Proposal

1. `issue-write` § Create: after `gh issue create` for a piece of a split, `addSubIssue(input: {issueId: <parent>, subIssueId: <piece>})`. After writing a `Depends on #N` line, one `addBlockedBy(input: {issueId: <this item>, blockingIssueId: <#N>})` per number named.
2. `issue-triage` § Apply, the split bullet and any ruling whose edit writes a dependency line: the same two calls, so a ruling never leaves a line without its relation.
3. `issue-next` § Skip: read `blockedBy(first: 50) { nodes { number state } }`, and for a parent `subIssues(first: 50) { nodes { number state } }`, in one `gh api graphql` per candidate, in place of the `gh issue view <N> --json state` walk. A `Depends on #N` line with no matching `blockedBy` node is reported as a malformed dependency, as an unresolvable number is.
4. `tests/test_payload.py` pins the three passages. No new script: the `gh api graphql` calls sit inline in the skill bodies.

Cost: three skill bodies, three pins, one commit.

## Acceptance

- `issue-triage` splits a parent into pieces → `gh api graphql` on the parent lists each piece under `subIssues.nodes` and `subIssuesSummary.total` counts them
- an item whose § Related carries `Depends on #M` → `blockedBy.nodes` on that item lists #M
- `issue-next` runs where the top item is blocked by an open issue → that item is skipped and reported with the blocker's number, read from `blockedBy`
- `issue-next` runs on an item whose `Depends on #M` line has no `blockedBy` node for #M → reported as a malformed dependency
- `bash tests/gate.sh` → green
- `bash tests/pressure.sh --only issue-next`, `--only issue-write`, `--only issue-triage` → PASS

## Related

- #53 — parked; GitHub issue enumeration and dependency handling.
- #65 — the `parked` and `blocked` labels: a label is out of the queue by decision, a relation is a fact the tracker holds.
- #49 — tracker-mutation authority.
- Out of scope: adding relations to items that exist today.
label: feature

title: 파일 업로드 보안 강화 (MIME/매직바이트 검증, 실행파일 차단, 경로순회 방지)
body:
## 배경
지금은 업로드 파일을 파일명 확장자(.pdf/.docx/.xlsx/.pptx)만 보고 허용함.
MIME 타입은 저장만 하고 검증 안 함(Swagger 문서에도 명시돼있음), 파일 내용(매직바이트)도
전혀 안 봐서, 확장자만 .pdf로 바꾸면 사실상 어떤 파일이든(실행파일 포함) 업로드가 통과됨.
파일명을 그대로 저장 키에 써서 경로순회(path traversal) 가능성도 있는지 확인 안 됨.

## 할 일
- [ ] MIME 타입 검증 — Content-Type이 허용 확장자와 실제로 맞는지 확인
- [ ] 매직바이트(파일 시그니처) 검증 — 파일 내용 앞부분을 읽어서 진짜 PDF/DOCX/XLSX/PPTX인지 확인
- [ ] 실행파일 차단 — 확장자 위장 여부와 무관하게, 매직바이트 기준으로 실행파일류(PE/ELF 등) 명시적 차단
- [ ] 파일명 sanitize — S3 저장 키 생성 시 원본 파일명에서 경로순회(`../`) 요소 제거/치환
- [ ] 저장소(S3) 접근권한 검토 — 버킷 정책/IAM 권한이 최소 권한 원칙을 따르는지 확인

## 참고
같은 업로드 처리 경로(RagIngestService)를 건드리는 작업이라 한 번에 묶어서 진행.

title: 水晶賭場：單人牌九撲克完整玩法（全萬用 Joker）
body:
## What to build

在既有水晶賭場加入單人「牌九撲克 Pai Gow Poker」。玩家與 bot 莊家各拿七張牌，選前墩兩張，剩餘五張為後墩；確認分牌後揭曉莊家，分別比較兩墩並以水晶結算。提供完整文字牌桌，沿用目前下注偏好、帳戶、單一進行中牌局、恢復、再開、流水及查帳流程。

本票包含規則、持久化、交易、Discord 文字互動與必要測試，是可獨立遊玩的完整功能。图片牌桌另票處理。使用者已核准拆票，並明確指定 Joker 可當任意牌，使所在墩組合最強。

## 規則決策

- 每局使用 52 張標準牌加一張 Joker，共 53 張；同一副牌不放回發給玩家及莊家各七張，發牌後持久保存，不因恢復或訊息失敗重抽。
- Joker 為全萬用牌，可代任意點數及花色，不限於 A 或補順子／同花；它是單一實體牌，不可同時出現在兩墩。替代值可與既有牌重複，因此允許四張同點數加 Joker 形成五條。
- 前墩只有對子及高牌：Joker 與任意自然牌組成該點數對子，例如 Joker＋K 為 KK，不是 AA。
- 後墩由強到弱：五條、同花順（皇家同花順為最高同花順）、四條、葫蘆、同花、順子、三條、兩對、對子、高牌。五條按點數比較，AAAA＋Joker 為最高五條。
- 在玩家選定分墩後，Joker 自動取該墩最強評分；玩家不可故意降低 Joker 評分規避倒墩。以牌型及完整踢腳序列比較，花色不分高低，天然牌與 Joker 組成的同等牌型沒有額外高低。
- 延用核准的特殊順子順序：AKQJ10 最高，A2345 第二，其後 KQJ109 到 23456；同花順使用相同序列。不可直接套用一般撲克的 wheel 最低規則。
- 後墩必須強於前墩。兩張與五張的跨墩合法性需用明確規則比較：先牌型，再同類有效點數／踢腳；比較共同長度相同後，五張後墩的剩餘踢腳使其較強。不可直接比較不一致的未定義 tuple。
- 倒墩、少選、多選、重複或不屬於玩家手牌的選牌不成立，只提示修正，不另扣款或判輸。
- 單墩完全同牌算莊家贏；玩家雙勝為勝，僅一墩勝為和，零墩勝為負。包含勝＋平＝和、負＋平＝負、平＋平＝負。
- 本 bot 明示採免抽水變體；勝／和／負返還累計下注的 2／1／0 倍。下注 100 的返還為 200／100／0，淨額為 +100／0／−100。不加邊注、玩家坐莊或額外加注。
- 莊家只依自身七張牌使用固定、版本化 House Way，不能依玩家選牌調整。以先前核准的 MotorCity 分牌表為起點，完整補齊全萬用 Joker、任意點數五條及多種可行解的固定優先序與平手處理；保存規則版本及最終分墩，避免重啟或改版後重新選擇。
- 自動分牌使用相同 House Way，僅讀玩家七張牌；它是固定分牌建議，不宣稱保證獲勝或數學最優。Joker 的「最強」指已選定墩的最強評分，不是預知莊家後挑選分墩。
- 傳統規則參考：https://www.motorcitycasino.com/tablegames.aspx?page=paigow 。該來源 Joker 有限制且收抽水；本票全萬用 Joker 與免抽水明確覆蓋來源，五條擴展到所有點數。

## Discord 流程

/賭場 → 牌九撲克 → 基本下注與倍率 → 開局 → 從七張具唯一索引的牌選兩張前墩 → 預覽前二後五及牌型 → 確認分牌 → 顯示雙方兩墩、逐墩勝負及總結算。
提供「自動分牌」填入建議；確認前可改選，改選不扣款。只能由面板主人操作。
分牌期限固定為開局後 120 秒；改選、自動分牌及重新 /賭場 均不延長期限。逾時按 House Way 自動分牌並結算，避免放棄不利牌局取得退款。
結果提供再來一局、修改下注、返回大廳；紀錄及莊家統計可辨識與篩選新遊戲識別。

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] 大廳入口到下注、手動／自動分牌、確認、結算、再開及查帳均可使用；完整文字顯示無須依賴圖片票。
- [x] 用決策表及固定牌例鎖定 House Way 全部路徑，包含無對、一對、多對、三條、葫蘆、順子／同花重疊、四條、任意點數五條及 Joker 多解；所有輸出均合法且 deterministic。
- [x] 以固定牌組驗證 Joker＋K＝KK、Joker 補非 A 三條／葫蘆／四條／順子／同花順、四張 7＋Joker＝五條 7、五條高於同花順，以及 Joker 位於不同墩與不可降級規避倒墩。
- [x] 驗證特殊順子順序、完整踢腳、跨墩合法性及九種單墩勝／負／平組合；每個實體牌 ID 只使用一次。
- [x] 重啟及重新 /賭場 保留原牌、選牌、規則版本與期限；莊家暗牌在確認或逾時結算前不進入文字、圖片投影、紀錄或日誌。
- [x] 沿用帳戶列鎖、跨遊戲每人單一 active 局、操作 token／版本與單次派彩。連點、重送、跨面板、再开及手動確認與逾時競態不重扣、不重派。
- [x] 扣款、發牌及持久狀態原子提交；結算、返還及流水原子提交。未知 COMMIT 結果先查證；網路／訊息失敗不退款，不可恢復狀態才作廢並全額退款一次。
- [x] 精確整數處理現有允許的大額下注；沿用基本下注與倍率約束。每局流水總和等於 returned − wager。
- [x] 如需 migration，採增量且可重跑方式，保留現有骰子與二十一點資料；更新遊戲識別、約束、查帳與文件，不能讓新遊戲被既有 else 分支當成骰子。
- [x] 執行有針對性的規則、互動與隔離資料庫交易測試；資料庫測試若跳過需明示，既有二十一點／18 豆仔核心流程不得回歸。

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Implementation status

本機 main 已完成實作，最新提交 5535b86；主要實作 13734d9，review 補強 df8ef88。完整套件 151 項測試通過，含隔離 PostgreSQL；補強固定牌例另行通過。驗證紀錄：docs/paigow-validation.md。提交目前保存在本機，尚未推送或部署。

title: [CuratedByDer][Enhance][Admin][FE] Redesign Delete Confirmation Modal
body:
### Summary

Redesign every delete-confirmation popup to match the new mockup (colors + layout). All delete confirmations in the app already route through one shared component — `src/components/ConfirmDeleteButton.tsx`, which exports `ConfirmDeleteDialog` and `ConfirmDeleteButton` — so this is a single-file redesign that updates every delete modal at once (books, toys, buyers, orders, batches, order payments, and the card variants in `BookCard`/`ToyCard`/`BuyerCard`/`OrderCard`). Frontend only.

### Problem

The current dialog (`ConfirmDeleteButton.tsx:49`) is the old minimal style: cream background `#F6F1E7`, small red-100 circle holding a `Trash2`, generic title `"Konfirmasi Hapus"`, plain description, and two flat buttons. It does not match the new design language used across the app (rose palette, rounded cards, explicit warning block) and reads as a generic browser-style confirm rather than a deliberate destructive action. The built-in close button (`ui/dialog.tsx:45`) is a dark slate circle, which also clashes with the mockup.

### Proposal

Rework the shared dialog to the mockup: warm near-white card, centered illustration (pink blob + red trash icon), large bold entity-specific title (`Hapus Buku?`, `Hapus Pembeli?`, `Hapus Mainan?`, `Hapus Order?`, `Hapus Batch?`, `Hapus Pembayaran?`), centered gray description with the entity name in quotes, a light-pink warning block (red `!` icon + "Tindakan ini tidak dapat dibatalkan." + "Data <entity> yang dihapus tidak akan bisa dikembalikan."), and two rounded-full/rounded-xl buttons: white outlined `Batal` + solid red `Hapus` with a trash icon. Support this from the existing prop surface so call sites only need text tweaks.

Concrete design tokens from the mockup:

- Card: warm near-white (`#FDF7F3`) rounded-2xl, wider padding, no visible border.
- Close button: light gray circle (`#EFEFEF`) with mid-gray `X` (`#4B5563`) — override the built-in `DialogPrimitive.Close` style or hide it and render a local close (per mockup).
- Illustration: light-pink blob (`#F9D2D8`) behind a rose/crimson `Trash2` (`#E1445A`). Generic version reused for all entities (the open-book doodle in the mockup is book-specific decoration) — keep it entity-agnostic unless told otherwise.
- Title: large, bold, near-black, centered.
- Description: gray (`#6B7280`), centered, entity name in double quotes.
- Warning block: `#FCE9EC` rounded-xl, red filled circle with `!` (`#E1445A`), bold black line + gray subtitle.
- Buttons: `Batal` = white bg, light border, dark text, rounded-xl; `Hapus` = solid red `#E02B3C`, white text, trash icon on the left, rounded-xl. Keep the existing pending/spinner state.
- Keep it mobile-first and width-capped (`w-[90%] max-w-*`) as today.

### High-level steps

1. Restyle `ConfirmDeleteDialog` in `src/components/ConfirmDeleteButton.tsx` to the mockup (card, close button, illustration, warning block, buttons).
2. Extend props for the new pieces — required: `title`, `description`; new optional: `warningTitle` + `warningText` (defaults so nothing breaks). Keep `label`/`pendingLabel` behavior.
3. Wire the close button so it still calls `onOpenChange(false)` and keeps Radix a11y (or override `ui/dialog.tsx`'s built-in close styling locally).
4. Update call sites only where copy should become entity-specific (titles → `Hapus Buku?` etc., warning text per entity); no logic changes.
5. Verify pending/loading, success modal, and `router.refresh()` flow still work unchanged.

### Existing result

Every delete confirmation shows the old cream dialog with a small red circle icon, generic `"Konfirmasi Hapus"` title, a plain description, and `Batal`/`Hapus` flat buttons. The dark-slate circular close button is the default from `ui/dialog.tsx`.

### Expected result

Every delete confirmation (books, toys, buyers, orders, batches, order payments, card variants) shows the new mockup design with consistent colors, an entity-specific bold title, a warning block that states the action cannot be undone and the data cannot be recovered, and the outlined/red button pair — on mobile and desktop.

### Checklist

- [ ] Only `src/components/ConfirmDeleteButton.tsx` (plus trivial copy edits at call sites) is touched — no logic/behavior regression.
- [ ] Warning block + entity-specific title/description render correctly for all 6 delete contexts.
- [ ] Pending state (spinner + `Menghapus...`) and disabled button preserved.
- [ ] Success/error modal flow (`useSuccessModal`) and `router.refresh()` still fire.
- [ ] Close (X), `Batal`, backdrop click, and Esc all cancel without deleting.
- [ ] Matches existing rose palette/rounded-card language; mobile-first at 375px.
- [ ] `tsc` and `eslint` clean.

### Acceptance criteria

- All delete-confirmation popups across the admin app share one redesigned component matching the mockup (colors, illustration, warning block, button pair).
- Titles are entity-specific (`Hapus Buku?`, `Hapus Mainan?`, `Hapus Pembeli?`, `Hapus Order?`, `Hapus Batch?`, `Hapus Pembayaran?`); the warning block names the entity being deleted.
- Deleting still works end-to-end (confirms, calls the action, shows the success modal, refreshes the list) and canceling never deletes.
- No visual regressions on mobile (375px) or desktop; type-check and lint pass.

title: Three competing mastery rules in one codebase: decide which is authoritative
body:
## Summary

There are three separate, mutually inconsistent implementations of "has this learner mastered this?" in the repo. They disagree about what mastery means, they were written by different contributors at different times, and nothing documents which one is authoritative.

## The three

**1. Bayesian Knowledge Tracing.** `client/src/bkt.js` and `server/lib/bkt.js`, added in `8ec90e12` (PR #49, 15 Jul 2026). A probabilistic model: mastery is a probability in `(0, 1)`, updated per opportunity with guess and slip parameters, smoothed so no single answer moves it more than about 11% of the remaining gap.

**2. LIL `masteryEngine`.** `server/lil/masteryEngine.js`, added in `c65bcde2` (08 Jul 2026, Learning Intelligence Layer). A binary rule, and a very permissive one:

```js
if (isCorrect) {
  record.incorrectStreak = 0;
  // Standard baseline mastery rule: mark completed on correct answer
  if (!record.isMastered) {
    record.isMastered = true;
```

One correct answer marks the concept mastered. Three consecutive wrong answers un-master it.

**3. Vachana mastery.** `client/src/vachana/VachanaMastery.js`. A third rule again: five consecutive correct to advance, three consecutive wrong to regress, persisted to `localStorage`, grounded in Bloom's mastery learning rather than BKT.

## Why this needs a decision

These do not just differ in tuning, they differ in kind. Under rule 2 a single lucky guess certifies a concept. Under rule 1 that same guess moves a probability by a few percent, which is the entire point of modelling `pGuess` at 0.25. A child can be "mastered" in one subsystem and nowhere near it in another, and the platform has no consistent answer to "what does this learner know".

It also blocks cleanup work: the de-duplication issue and the unwired-`SkillMasteryState` issue both have to assume an answer to "which rule wins" before they can finish.

## Not intern-ready

This is an architecture call, not a task. Filing it so the question is tracked somewhere rather than living in three files that never reference each other.

## What a resolution looks like

- One documented mastery rule for the platform, or an explicit, written statement that different learning modes intentionally use different rules and why.
- If BKT wins, `masteryEngine.js` either delegates to it or is retired, and `VachanaMastery` is either brought in line or explicitly carved out.
- The decision recorded in the repo, not only in chat, so the next contributor does not add a fourth rule.

title: Decide plugin-manager strategy — keep built-in manager vs. adopt a forked slopsmith-update-manager
body:
## Context

`slopsmith-update-manager` (https://github.com/get-flashbacks/slopsmith-update-manager, currently a byrongamatos-upstream fork) is a considerably more capable plugin manager than what's built into feedBack-desktop today:

| Capability | Desktop's built-in Plugin Manager | slopsmith-update-manager |
|---|---|---|
| Install from GitHub URL | Yes | Yes |
| Update Git clones | Yes | Yes |
| Update bundled plugins | No | Yes, via writable overrides |
| Works without Git installed | No | Yes |
| Detect available versions | No | Yes |
| Downgrade/pin versions | No | Yes |
| Browse plugin registry | No | Yes |
| Storage usage and cache controls | No | Yes |
| Update packaged desktop/core | Separate desktop updater | No (hidden in desktop mode) |
| Private repositories | Potentially, through configured Git | No documented authentication |

The one feature actually relevant to a packaged fork: bundled (read-only, inside the app bundle) plugins can be updated by writing a copy into the writable user-plugins directory, which loads in preference to the bundled copy. That lets a user pick up a get-flashbacks plugin update without waiting for a whole new desktop installer.

## The decision this issue tracks

Do **not** ship both management interfaces unchanged — they'd overlap confusingly (a "Plugins" screen using Git clones, and an "Update Manager" screen using downloaded ZIPs + marker files, both visible, doing similar things differently). Before adopting `slopsmith-update-manager`, decide:

1. Keep the desktop's built-in manager as the only visible plugin-management UI, and bundle fixed plugin versions (simpler, reproducible — **recommended for the initial packaged release**).
2. Fork and adopt `slopsmith-update-manager` as the *single* visible plugin-management interface, either removing the desktop's built-in `plugin_manager` UI entirely or replacing it with a link into the adopted plugin.

If (2) is chosen, prerequisite work is tracked separately in `get-flashbacks/slopsmith-update-manager` (see that repo's "Fork prerequisites for get-flashbacks adoption" issue) — repointing the registry/core-owner/fallback-heuristic away from `byrongamatos`, giving every bundled plugin a `repository`/`url` field it can resolve against, hardening the desktop-mode detection, and adding auth support if any private get-flashbacks plugin (e.g. `feedback-plugin-chordr`, if private) needs to be updatable through it.

## Responsibility split (if adopted)

Keep these separate regardless of which UI wins:

- **feedBack-desktop's own updater** (Velopack/Linux updater) → Electron shell, core, Python, native audio engine, the bundled baseline. Unaffected either way.
- **Update Manager** (if adopted) → optional plugin installs and writable plugin overrides only. Should never touch the packaged desktop/core update path — this is already how the plugin behaves upstream (core-update UI is hidden when `SLOPSMITH_PLUGINS_DIR`/desktop mode is detected), and that separation should hold after the fork.

## Recommendation

Ship the existing built-in manager for the initial packaged release. Revisit adoption for a later release once the prerequisite fork work (tracked in `slopsmith-update-manager`) is done and the two-UI overlap question above is actually decided, not deferred by shipping both.

title: Is zot show --json output meant to feed zot item create?
body:
Surfaced while scoping #116. Today the answer is no, and nothing says so.

## The gap

`zot show --json` emits a zotgo DTO. `zot item create` accepts Zotero-native item JSON and passes it through verbatim. The two shapes differ:

| DTO | Zotero native |
|---|---|
| `type` | `itemType` |
| `creators[].type` | `creators[].creatorType` |
| `tags[].name` + `automatic` | `tags[].tag` + `type` |
| `parentKey` | `parentItem` |

and the DTO carries derived fields a write never accepts: `parsedDate`, `creatorSummary`, `numChildren`, `children`, `dateAdded`, `dateModified`.

So piping `zot show --json | jq .data` into `zot item create` produces an item with **no `itemType`**. The dry-run shows it plainly:

```
$ zot show KEY --json | jq '.data' | zot item create --library me --dry-run
Target: My Library — ...
  + —: Why bioreactor vendors are betting on single-use
```

That `—` is the missing type.

## Why it matters

It is the natural thing to try. `zot show --raw | jq '.item.data'` is the form that works, which means the round-trippable path is the *unversioned* one explicitly outside the DTO contract, while the versioned, documented output is the one that does not round-trip. That is backwards from what a user would guess.

It also blocks the cheap fix in #116: the children signal exists only in the DTO, so a create-time warning is only reachable if the DTO path works.

## The question

Three positions, all defensible:

1. **Explicitly not round-trippable.** The DTO is a read contract for humans and scripts; writes take Zotero's vocabulary because that is what Zotero validates against. Document it and move on. Cheapest, and arguably honest — a display DTO is not a write schema.
2. **Round-trippable, via normalization in `item create`.** Accept either shape: map the four renamed fields, drop the derived ones, warn about what is dropped. Makes `show | create` work, unlocks #116, and makes the DTO the single vocabulary a user has to learn.
3. **Round-trippable, via a dedicated flag** (`item create --from-dto`, or similar). Keeps the default strict and the conversion explicit, at the cost of a flag users must discover.

Position 2 is the most useful and the largest commitment: it makes every future DTO field addition a write-path question too.

## Not urgent

No behaviour is broken — the raw path works and is what the tooling uses. This is about whether a reasonable expectation should be made true. Worth settling before 1.0 fixes the contract, but not a blocker for the rc.

title: Should the default grant scope be every non-destructive operation?
body:
Suggestion 3 from #114, split out because it amends a stated rule in `docs/design/write-authority.md` rather than being a behaviour fix.

## The observation

From the #114 report: a lease was needed for a single `item.create`. The default grant supplied eight operations.

```
operations: item.create, item.patch, item.replace, collection.create,
            collection.rename, collection.move, tag.add, tag.remove,
            attachment.import
```

`item.replace` is a destructive full overwrite in everything but name — Q3 says exactly that, calling it "destructive full overwrite, must be separable from `patch`" — yet it is in the default because it does not *delete*.

## The current rule

`defaultGrantOperations()` grants every operation not in `destructiveOperations`, where destructive means **can lose data**. Q8 recently added a second exclusion, **nondeterministic target**, for the `ingest.*` family.

So the rule is now: withhold what can lose data, and withhold what writes somewhere the minter cannot predict.

## The question

Does "can lose data" draw the line in the right place for `item.replace`?

A full replace cannot lose the *item*, but it can lose every field the new payload omits. Against `item.patch` in the same default, a caller that only ever needed to patch is carrying the ability to overwrite wholesale.

Three shapes worth weighing:

1. **Leave it.** The rule is mechanical and the prompt prints the full list before anyone confirms. Adding exceptions makes the default harder to reason about than the thing it protects against.
2. **Move `item.replace` to the withheld set.** Smallest change. Needs an honest name for why — it is not data loss under the current definition, so either the definition widens or a third category appears, and Q8 already added one category this week.
3. **Narrow the default much further** — say `item.create`, `item.patch`, `tag.add`, `tag.remove` — on the grounds that a default should cover the common case rather than the maximal safe one, with everything else named explicitly.

## Worth noting

Q3 already anticipated this tension: it records that the common "clean up metadata" grant is "therefore verbose", and defers wildcards and presets as additive sugar. A narrower default and a preset are arguably the same feature approached from opposite ends.

No action implied. This is a decision for `write-authority.md`, and it should be resolved there as a numbered question or closed as settled.

title: [Explore] MCP server exposing PowerNetbox to AI agents
body:
> **Exploratory.** No release commitment - this issue exists to hold the idea and the evidence, not to schedule work.

## Rationale

Microsoft's [2026 investments post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/powershell/powershell-openssh-and-dsc-team-investments-for-2026/) commits the PowerShell team to "develop a team supported Model Context Protocol (MCP) server" for PowerShell 7.7, with an explicit safety-and-security-first framing. That is a signal about where module consumption is heading: AI agents calling tools, not just humans calling cmdlets.

PowerNetbox is unusually well positioned for this - 575 cmdlets already wrap the full NetBox REST surface, with parameter validation, version gating and centralised error handling. An MCP server would be a thin projection over work that is already done.

## Sketch

A small server exposing a curated, **read-only** tool set over the existing cmdlets:

- `netbox_search_devices`, `netbox_get_device`, `netbox_search_ip_addresses`, `netbox_get_prefix_utilisation`, `netbox_search_circuits`, ...
- Sessions and credentials handled by `Connect-NBAPI` / the session object, never passed through the model.
- Write operations deliberately excluded in a first cut. If they are ever added, they belong behind an explicit opt-in switch and `ShouldProcess`.

## Open questions

- **Host runtime.** Wait for the official PowerShell MCP server (7.7) and register tools with it, or ship a standalone server? Waiting is almost certainly right - building our own transport now means rewriting it later.
- **Packaging.** Separate repo/module (`PowerNetbox.MCP`) rather than bloating the main module's dependency surface.
- **Safety.** A NetBox instance is a map of the network. Read-only is still sensitive; scoping and token permissions need thought before anything ships.

## Next step

Re-evaluate when the PowerShell 7.7 MCP work reaches preview. Until then: no code.

Part of #481.

title: Rename the agent developer-standard to developer, so the bare name is the Opus default
body:
## Goal

The bare agent name is the Opus default and the suffix is the tier modifier: `developer` (Opus, `effort: xhigh`), `developer-trivial` (Sonnet), `developer-complex` (Fable). `developer-standard` no longer exists anywhere in the repository or in `~/.claude/agents`. The researchers keep both modifiers, because no Opus researcher exists. The tier label `standard` on issues is unchanged.

## Why

The Opus developer carries a tier suffix while the Opus reviewer does not:

- `claude/agents/developer-standard.md:2` — `name: developer-standard`, with `model: opus` at `:5` and `effort: xhigh` at `:6`.
- `claude/agents/reviewer.md:2` — `name: reviewer`, `model: opus` at `:5`; `claude/agents/reviewer-complex.md:2` — `name: reviewer-complex`, `model: fable` at `:5`. The reviewer pair is already bare-name-is-default plus one tier modifier.
- `claude/skills/deliver/references/tiers.md:30` — the `standard` routing row of the Claude Code routing table names `developer-standard` in the Developer column beside `reviewer` in the Reviewer column, a suffixed developer next to a bare reviewer.

## Proposal

Rename `claude/agents/developer-standard.md` to `claude/agents/developer.md` and set its `name:` field to `developer`; `model: opus` and `effort: xhigh` stay as they are. Then update every reference site:

- `claude/agents/developer-standard.md:2` — the file name and the `name:` field.
- `claude/skills/deliver/references/tiers.md:30` — the `standard` routing row.
- `tests/test_payload.py:72` — `DEVELOPER_AGENTS`.
- `tests/test_payload.py:77` — `EXPECTED_AGENT_MODELS`.
- `tests/test_payload.py:86` — `EXPECTED_AGENTS`.
- `tests/test_payload.py:97` — `TIER_ROUTING_ROWS`.

`EXPECTED_AGENT_SKILLS` at `tests/test_payload.py:74` is derived from `DEVELOPER_AGENTS` and needs no separate edit, and the `effort: xhigh` assertion at `tests/test_payload.py:347` selects agents by model, not by name, so it needs none either. The `prune` call at `apply.sh:65` removes the stale `~/.claude/agents/developer-standard.md` link and the loop at `apply.sh:50` creates `developer.md`, so `./apply.sh` handles the relink with no change to the script. The chat's memory outside the repository is the chat's to update.

Cost: one rename, six reference sites, one commit, one relink.

## Acceptance

- `ls ~/.claude/agents` after `./apply.sh` → `developer.md`, `developer-trivial.md`, `developer-complex.md`, and no `developer-standard.md`.
- `grep -rn "developer-standard" claude tests README.md` → 0 hits.
- The `standard` row of the routing table in `claude/skills/deliver/references/tiers.md` names `developer`.
- `bash tests/gate.sh` → green.
- `./apply.sh --check` → ok.

## Related

- #66 — the reviewer split that established bare name for the Opus reviewer and a `-complex` modifier.
- #14 — the three developer tiers and the tier routing table this renames a row of.
- The researchers keep both modifiers, and the `tier: standard` issue label is out of scope.

title: docs: clarify double-quoted string fallback is intentionally unsupported (SQL standard identifier semantics)
body:
## Description
Users familiar with MySQL (default non-ANSI mode) or SQLite may expect `"1.9.5"` to be silently reinterpreted as a string literal when it doesn't resolve to a real column/table name. db-core's parser does not do this: double quotes are *always* parsed as identifiers, per the SQL standard. When the identifier doesn't resolve, this correctly produces an error rather than silently guessing the user meant a string.

This is **not a bug** — it's the strict standard-conformant reading. SQLite's behavior is a documented misfeature kept only for backwards compatibility (https://sqlite.org/quirks.html#dblquote), and MySQL only does this outside `ANSI_QUOTES` sql_mode. Both are compatibility carve-outs, not the ANSI baseline db-core targets.

This ticket exists to document the decision so it isn't "fixed" into non-conformant behavior later, and to make the error message clearer about *why* this happens.

## Complexity
**Estimate:** small
**Reasoning:** No parser behavior change; scope is an ADR/spec note plus improving the parse error message to mention the standard-identifier reasoning (optional).

## Context
Related tokenizer logic: `src/parser/row/tokenizer.rs`. Confusion originates from cross-tool comparison, not from any actual defect in db-core.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ADR or spec note added stating double-quoted strings are always identifiers (no silent string-literal fallback), citing SQLite/MySQL as the intentionally-not-followed precedent
- [ ] (Optional) Parser error message for unresolved double-quoted identifiers hints that string literals must use single quotes
- [ ] No behavior change to the parser itself

## Additional Notes
Won't-fix from a "support the fallback" angle — kept open only for the documentation/error-message follow-up.

---
🤖 *Analysis by Claude*

body:
I noticed on my real 16C that if I store something other than a zero in **I**, then switch to Float mode, and try to recall it (or it's contents), I get an ERROR 6. (Page 57 of the manual shows that it's normal behavior.)  JRPN16 does not have this limitation.

Example:
`HEX`
`1, STO I`
`f, FLOAT .`
`RCL I` -> **Error 6**

It seems that it, when in Float mode, it stores the **I** in using the same big-endian BCD format as the other float values. EX:
`f, Float .`
`1,  STO I`
`HEX`
`RCL I` -> **1000000000000 h**

So, maybe it does the reverse of the conversion when switching _TO_ float mode which results in an unusable Index register number? I don't really understand the 68-bit part of it though, maybe that's used for non-floating point.

title: `param_exists` fails when requested query param has no value
body:
The following should work but does not:

```
pook.get("https://example.com").param_exists("x")
urlopen("https://example.com/?x")
```

This is because the query param matcher returns `false` here:

https://github.com/h2non/pook/blob/fac40e9f571152ba09bc16954548ce51d590ccea/src/pook/matchers/query.py#L14-L15

It should check `key in req_query` in addition to None. Falling back to an empty string in that method when `key in req_query and req_query[key] is None` _might_ be okay, but it could interfere with other expectations. It would be safer to augment `param_exists` to correctly handle the present-but-None case, potentially by using a simpler matcher class altogether instead of overloading the existing `QueryMatcher` and abusing the regex matching.

## Describe the bug

refs #1006

_Reported by @SMotaal, and we investigated it together._

Using `*.endo.localhost` is not adequately supported under Safari for macOS 16.2.

Unlike Firefox and Chrome, which always use their own HTTPS DNS servers that support `*.localhost` in an RFC-compliant way, Safari uses the system default DNS resolver, which is probably backed by whichever Internet Service Provider is in use.

Not all such providers support `*.localhost`, which makes Safari unusable for the current Endo Daemon.

title: Update World Generation to be Rentrant
body:
Currently, world generation works (very) roughly like this:

1. Terraform each continent
2. Randomize all of the items into all the places
3. Check if the seed is beatable. If it is, succeed. If we have done this more than a certain limit of times, GOTO 1: If we are under that limit, GOTO 2.

The problem with this is that some biomes / settings are more likely to fail than others. If we are 1/10 to find a working west, and 1/10 to find a working east, this setup is 1/100 to find a working set of continents as a whole. For bad biome sets, this becomes too much to bear and the generation takes forever. A better system works like this:

1. Terraform each continent
2. Randomize all of the items into all the places
3. Check if the seed is beatable, If so succeed
4. Find the list of continents that had failures in the most/majority/any of the item shuffles, re-randomize those biomes.
5. Goto 2.

This way if the west and east are very likely to be unbeatable no matter what the shuffle, they can be rerolled. If a biome is very likely to succeed, we don't need to waste effort building it over and over again. And the big winner, if a biome is unlikely to succeed but we found a good one that does, we can hold onto it and not throw it out the window. The hope is that we can turn 1/10 independent events for 1/100 to 2 different 1/10 checks that stop when they succeed, which is an order of magnitude gain on the most painful seeds.

## Issue Description

During the regression analysis of the Melbourne housing data (file: `3_regression_model.py`), several areas of concern were identified in the OLS regression results that may impact the model's reliability and accuracy. These need to be investigated and addressed to enhance the robustness of our findings.

### Identified Concerns

1. **Non-Normality of Residuals**:
   - The Jarque-Bera test suggests that the residuals from the regression model are not normally distributed. This non-normality can affect the reliability of the hypothesis tests conducted on the model's coefficients.

2. **Mild Autocorrelation in Residuals**:
   - The Durbin-Watson statistic indicates a presence of mild autocorrelation in the residuals. This autocorrelation can violate the OLS assumption of independent errors, potentially leading to biased estimates.

3. **Potential Multicollinearity Among Predictors**:
   - The regression model's high condition number points towards potential multicollinearity among the predictors. Multicollinearity can make it difficult to ascertain the effect of individual predictors and might inflate the variance of coefficient estimates.

### Required Actions

- **Investigation and Addressing Non-Normality**: Explore data transformations or alternative modeling approaches to handle non-normal residuals.
- **Autocorrelation Check and Remediation**: Further analyze the residuals for autocorrelation. Consider time series analysis techniques if necessary.
- **Multicollinearity Assessment and Mitigation**: Use Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) analysis to identify multicollinearity. Depending on findings, consider removing highly correlated predictors, combining them, or applying regularization techniques.

### Goal

The objective is to refine and improve the regression model to ensure that it meets the assumptions of OLS regression and provides reliable and accurate insights into the Melbourne housing market.


There's a lot of syntax noise around the actual message context, so it seems like it would be easier to define these messages if they were defined as format strings instead. This would also allow the actual messages to not be hard-coded on the server side, and instead be loaded from a translation file or something by clients.

Some compile-time checking would be lost, but flexibility would be gained, allowing for translations of the game to other languages, and potentially reducing the amount of data sent from the server.

One possible format string version of the above message:
```
%name.1% throws %name.2%, but %name.3% moves out of the way just before %they.2% %hits/hit.2% %them.3%.
```

Sections enclosed in `%` denote tokens. `name` for entity names, forms of "they" for pronouns, and `a/b` for "a if the entity's pronoun is singular, b if it's plural".

The `.1`/`.2`/`.3` parts denote which entity to look at. So for this message, a list of `[context.performing_entity, context.item, context.target]` would be provided to build the final string.

It might be better to assign names to entities rather than just numbers, though that would increase the syntax noise a bit.
